dataset.censoring_treatment: Loans active at the panel edge are censored there. The discrete-time hazard likelihood contributes only the months actually observed, so censored loans contribute correctly rather than being dropped (biases hazards down) or treated as negatives (biases them down harder).

kaplan_meier_overall.censoring_note: Loans still active at the panel edge are censored there, not treated as non-events. Treating them as negatives would bias every hazard downward.

log_rank.interpretation: No significant separation between segment curves.

kaplan_meier_by_credit_band.censoring_note: Loans still active at the panel edge are censored there, not treated as non-events. Treating them as negatives would bias every hazard downward.

markov_baseline.note: No covariates. Any lift the hazard model shows over this is what features buy.

model_evaluation.concordance_index_note: Computed on active-only rows (Prepaid/Closed excluded). Terminal rows are correctly ranked low for default but distort the C-index when included.

integrated_brier_score.note: IPCW-corrected; lower is better. 0.25 is the uninformative reference.

baseline_comparison.markov_note: The Markov chain has no covariates. Any C-index above 0.5 for the hazard model is what the feature set buys over average portfolio behaviour.

confusion_profile.cost_note: A false negative is a missed default; a false positive is wasted reviewer capacity. The operating threshold encodes which the business is willing to trade.

The dimensions analysed here (state, credit band, servicer) are proxy-adjacent operational cuts, not protected classes. They are reported as diagnostics only and are deliberately not optimised against: tuning a model to equalise a metric across a proxy, without the real attribute, can increase real-world disparate impact rather than reduce it.
